classification.difficultyReason: Choose a general linear remainder from the divisor degree, evaluate at its roots and solve the resulting two simultaneous equations.

content.prompt:
The polynomial $P(x)$ is divided by $(x-1)(x+4)$.
Find the remainder if $P(1)=10$ and $P(-4)=-5$.

answer.short: $R(x)=3x+7$. Write $R(x)=ax+b$ and use the divisor's roots.
answer.worked:
The divisor has degree 2, so write the remainder as $ax+b$.
$$P(x)=(x-1)(x+4)Q(x)+ax+b.$$
$$\begin{align*}P(1)&=a+b=10,\\P(-4)&=-4a+b=-5.\end{align*}$$
Subtracting the second equation from the first:
$$\begin{align*}5a&=15,\\a&=3.\end{align*}$$
Substituting into $a+b=10$:
$$\begin{align*}3+b&=10,\\b&=7,\\R(x)&=3x+7.\end{align*}$$
